provenance: LLM-backend-derived + deterministic-checked (Phase 16/17 inverted boundary) — NOT a ship typology config. The LLM backend read the source and EXTRACTED the 16 enumerated financial red-flag indicators (the thematic list under 'Such financial red flag indicators may include:', NOT the upstream 'representative types of illicit activity' typology overview); the deterministic gate GROUNDS each verbatim `flag` in the source md within the red-flag region + checks the cover×data matrix. This advisory is footnote-heavy (markitdown interleaves page-break footnote runs mid-flag), so each `flag` is a CONTIGUOUS grounded span — a clause split across a footnote page break (e.g. IND-01's '(2)' continuation) is dropped, never bridged across the interruption. build_rec follows the cover×data matrix (build_rec_category). Coverage/data values are ILLUSTRATIVE (vision demo).

indicators.section: Representative types of illicit activity — Unnecessary services
indicators.flag: Ordering or submitting claims for expensive tests or services that do not test for COVID-19, oftentimes in conjunction with COVID-19 testing, such as medically unnecessary and expensive respiratory testing, allergy testing, genetic testing, narcotics screening, or whole-body health assessments,
indicators.red_flag: Provider claims for medically-unnecessary high-cost ancillary tests bundled to COVID testing
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D14 (Government-program enrollment & eligibility data), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.section: Representative types of illicit activity — Billing schemes
indicators.flag: Billing for services not provided, or overbilling (e.g., upcoding or unbundling), when administering or processing COVID-19 testing and treatments.
indicators.red_flag: Phantom-billing / upcoding-unbundling claim inflation
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D14 (Government-program enrollment & eligibility data), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.section: Representative types of illicit activity — Kickbacks
indicators.flag: Paying service providers or purported marketing organizations an illegal kickback or bribe in exchange for ordering, or arranging for the ordering of, services and testing.
indicators.red_flag: Marketing-labeled kickback / bribe-for-referral disbursements
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D5 (Transaction narrative / free-text fields), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.section: Representative types of illicit activity — Health care technology schemes
indicators.flag: False and fraudulent representations about COVID-19 testing, treatments, or cures are used to defraud insurance carriers and to perpetrate fraud on the financial markets by defrauding investors.
indicators.red_flag: Investor-facing false-cure representations (market + insurer fraud)
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C19 (Adverse-media / OSINT & web-presence verification); data D13.

indicators.section: Representative types of illicit activity — Telefraud and telehealth schemes
indicators.flag: Collecting beneficiaries’ personally identifiable information (PII), including Medicare information.
indicators.red_flag: Beneficiary-PII harvesting for fraudulent telehealth claims
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D14 (Government-program enrollment & eligibility data), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.section: Representative types of illicit activity — Fraudulently obtaining relief funds
indicators.flag: Filing false claims and applications for Federal relief funds,
indicators.red_flag: False federal relief-fund claims with health-care nexus
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D14 (Government-program enrollment & eligibility data), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.section: Representative types of illicit activity — Identity theft leading to additional
indicators.flag: Targeting beneficiaries for their PII and then using the stolen PII to commit COVID-19-related fraud against health care benefit programs.
indicators.red_flag: Stolen-PII identity-theft feeding benefit-program fraud
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D14 (Government-program enrollment & eligibility data), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.section: Additional, medically unnecessary services or billing schemes
indicators.flag: A COVID-19-related health care service provider’s business account has unusual transaction activities, such as payments for personal or medically irrelevant expenses (e.g., payments to automobile dealers, travel agents, or retailers of luxury goods).
indicators.red_flag: Business account spending on luxury / personal non-medical MCCs
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D4 (Card & merchant-category (MCC) transaction data), not currently held → source data first.

build_logic.logic: Flag a card or account whose merchant-category spend distribution shifts toward high-risk or atypical MCCs for the customer's segment, escalating when spend concentrates in cash-equivalent categories such as gift cards, prepaid, or money-services merchants.
build_logic.window: rolling 60 days vs segment MCC baseline
build_logic.source: card authorization/settlement feed enriched with MCC reference
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert â AML analyst review gate

indicators.flag: Following the COVID-19 public health emergency declaration, personal or business accounts, especially ones that did not previously receive health care-related payments, begin receiving steep increases in health care benefit program or health insurance payments.
indicators.red_flag: No-history account onset of steep benefit/insurer inflows
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C6 (Transaction-velocity & dormancy / baseline-deviation monitoring).

indicators.flag: A purported health care service provider’s account receives health care benefit program or health insurance payments related to COVID-19 services, and then individuals immediately withdraw the funds in a manner that is not typical for health care businesses (e.g., cashier’s checks, cash withdrawals, certain types of Automated Clearing House (ACH) transfers, or domestic and international wire transfers).
indicators.red_flag: Inbound benefit credit → atypical immediate pass-through withdrawal
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C2 (Rapid pass-through / flow-through (receive-and-forward) detection).

indicators.flag: After the COVID-19 public health emergency determination, a purported health care provider’s account does not receive small-dollar check deposits, payments from merchant fee servicers, or cash payments from patients that would indicate patient copayments.  This may indicate the absence of actual business activity.
indicators.red_flag: Absent copay / merchant-fee inflows (no real patient activity)
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D1 (Core transaction monitoring (deposit/account ledger)), not currently held → source data first.

build_logic.logic: Flag a business account whose transaction inflows are disproportionate to its declared revenue, headcount, payroll, or operating-expense footprint relative to industry peers, escalating when revenue appears decoupled from any observable operational activity.
build_logic.window: rolling 90 days vs declared profile and peer cohort
build_logic.source: business deposit ledger joined to KYC business profile + industry peer benchmarks
build_logic.route: Tier-2 alert â AML analyst review gate

indicators.flag: A newly formed health care business account has a volume or type of payment that seems inconsistent with expected levels of activity for such an account.
indicators.red_flag: Newly-formed account activity inconsistent with peer baseline
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C1 (Customer-profile / out-of-pattern transaction monitoring); data D1.

indicators.flag: The physical location of a purported medical facility receiving reimbursements for COVID-19-related health care services or relief funds is non-existent, a residential address, a commercial mail receiving agency address (e.g., a UPS Store address), or another non-office building address
indicators.red_flag: Provider registered to non-existent / residential / CMRA address
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C13 (Account-opening / KYC risk profiling).

indicators.flag: The purported laboratory, health care service provider, or medical service personnel or their counterparties appear to have a minimal web presence, or one that begins around the time of the COVID-19 public health emergency declaration.
indicators.red_flag: Minimal / newly-created web presence for provider
indicators.rationale: Partially covered by C19 (Adverse-media / OSINT & web-presence verification); data D13.

indicators.flag: the physical location of a purported medical facility receiving payments for health care services or relief funds is far from the physical location of the majority of its patients or the providers purported to be practicing there, unless the facility is providing appropriate telehealth services
indicators.red_flag: Provider-patient geographic mismatch absent telehealth basis
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C20 (Cross-border / high-risk-jurisdiction & corridor anomaly detection).

indicators.flag: a health care service provider’s or other business account begins having overly complex, medical-related transactions involving multiple counterparties indicative of possible structuring, layering, kickbacks, or fraudulent medical claims.
indicators.red_flag: Overly-complex multi-counterparty layering / structuring pattern
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C3 (Multi-originator funnel-in / fan-out network detection).

indicators.flag: A health care service provider’s account makes frequent or unusually large payments recorded as advertising or marketing expenses, or makes recurring round-dollar payments to one or multiple individuals in a manner inconsistent with its payroll-related withdrawals.  The payments may reference “director fees,” “consulting fees,” “marketing,” or “business process outsourcing.”
indicators.red_flag: Round-dollar marketing/consulting-memo payouts off payroll baseline
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D5 (Transaction narrative / free-text fields), not currently held → source data first.

indicators.flag: A health care service provider starts receiving payments from laboratories and health care services companies, but there is no financial documentation (e.g., operating expense payments) that the provider rendered legitimate services.
indicators.red_flag: Inbound lab/provider payments with no service-cost footprint
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D1 (Core transaction monitoring (deposit/account ledger)), not currently held → source data first.

build_logic.logic: Flag a business account whose transaction inflows are disproportionate to its declared revenue, headcount, payroll, or operating-expense footprint relative to industry peers, escalating when revenue appears decoupled from any observable operational activity.
build_logic.window: rolling 90 days vs declared profile and peer cohort
build_logic.source: business deposit ledger joined to KYC business profile + industry peer benchmarks
build_logic.route: Tier-2 alert â AML analyst review gate

indicators.flag: An account with no previous known association with providing health care services, receives an unexpected or excessive COVID-19-related payment that appears to be the CARES Act’s Provider Relief Fund or the PPP-HCEA payments.  Shortly after the account receives the deposit, an individual(s) withdraws the funds via large cash withdrawals, cashier’s checks, wires to an overseas account, transfers to personal accounts, or payments for non-business expenses.
indicators.red_flag: No-nexus relief-fund credit → rapid cash / overseas-wire drawdown
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C2 (Rapid pass-through / flow-through (receive-and-forward) detection).

indicators.flag: An account previously associated with providing health care services but that has not been recently active or appears to be defunct, receives an unexpected or excessive COVID-19-related payment that appears to be the CARES Act’s Provider Relief Fund or the PPP-HCEA payments.
indicators.red_flag: Dormant / defunct provider account receives unexpected relief fund
indicators.rationale: Already covered by C6 (Transaction-velocity & dormancy / baseline-deviation monitoring).

indicators.flag: An account holder receives a substantial amount of reimbursements from health care benefit programs or health insurance companies for services rendered at the same time that the account holder receives COVID-19-related unemployment insurance payments.
indicators.red_flag: Concurrent provider-reimbursement and unemployment-benefit inflows
indicators.rationale: Gap; requires D14 (Government-program enrollment & eligibility data), not currently held → source data first.
